objective: Harden the CI quality pipeline with explicit dependency-gated sequencing, complete format coverage, runtime smoke validation, test/coverage artifacts, and dependency-change review.

baseline.description: Core CI quality jobs execute independently and a final gate aggregates their results.

evidence: The dependency graph now gates each quality stage on the preceding stage.
Ruff format validation now covers the complete src and tests trees.
Runtime smoke validation covers the CLI, API, and worker entry points.
Coverage and JUnit test reports are uploaded as CI artifacts.
Dependency Review is enforced for pull requests targeting main.
validation.blocker: Post-change CI must execute successfully before this lifecycle stage is finalized.

root_causes: Quality jobs were siblings with only the final aggregate gate depending on all of them.
Dependent validation could therefore execute despite an earlier unrelated failure.

findings: CI stages should form an explicit dependency graph when later stages consume the confidence established by earlier stages.
The final gate remains useful as an aggregate invariant even when execution is sequential.
Runtime entry-point smoke checks catch packaging or startup regressions that package import checks alone cannot detect.
Machine-readable CI artifacts improve post-failure diagnosis without changing scientific behavior.

open_blockers: Repository branch protection / required status checks must be configured on main before merge governance is complete.
